audit.why: 53.71% over 1255 games at 5.5/10 EVEN fits the kits: Lux owns levels 1-2 on range (E 1100 / Q 1175 vs Twofold Hex 900) and loses from 6 onward to two blinks plus spirit sustain.
audit.corrected: Early lane Lux, levels 3-5 skill, level 6 onward Aurora; she is the side-lane and teamfight threat because she flanks.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read a blanket 'Skill' while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Lux, Lux, Skill, Skill, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora. The page rendered a flat chart against a chart that actually moves.
audit.why: Both other sources agree, and the kits back them: she has no mobility at level 1-2, gains Across the Veil, then Between Worlds at 6 gives a second blink that beats an immobile mage.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side and [1].side -> Lux; [2] and [3] left Skill; [4], [5], [6].side -> Aurora. Each moved row's why rewritten in the same group. win[N] already matches on every row so no content edit is proposed (a no-op would be rejected and would sink the group).

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated that Across the Veil leaves her invisible on landing, that The Weirding is a second escape (a backward hop, 15s at rank 1), or that Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell and attack she lands.
audit.why: Those three are the whole reason Lux's chip pattern stops working. The old text carried only a generic 'track her hop' template with no cooldown and no mechanic.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Across the Veil 22s->18s, The Weirding 15s and Between Worlds 140s at rank 1; feeding and ahead now name Oblivion Orb against her passive healing; dontsFull[0].d states the 900-vs-1100 range gap that decides extended trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names: spikes[0].text called her W 'Across the Sand' and spikes[1].text called her R 'The Weystone'.
audit.why: Riot's kit lists W as Across the Veil and R as Between Worlds. The packet flagged the first; the second was not flagged and is equally wrong.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with the real names, and the real cooldowns (22s W, 140s R at rank 1) folded in.

audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns and it held only prose about 'forward steps'.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three of her cooldowns at real ranks.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing anywhere on the page against a passive that heals off every damaging spell and attack.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration turns Lux's chip-and-back pattern into free sustain for Aurora; without Grievous Wounds the poke plan does not accumulate.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb named in breakdown.feeding and ahead.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED), dosFull[2].d claimed a 'fifteen-second' Across the Veil that does not exist, and dontsFull[0].d called a female enemy 'they'.
audit.why: Titles promised the shield timing, the root discipline and the close-range trade; the bodies said something else, and the magnitude was invented.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten to their own titles with real numbers; Aurora is confirmed female in champ-gender.js.

edits.after: Prismatic Barrier is 12s at rank 1 — spend it on her Q recast pulling the curse back, not on the first missile that touches you.

edits.before: Aurora wins by landing Across the Veil (Hop), denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Aurora wins by blinking onto you with Across the Veil, healing the chip back off her spirits, and killing you before Q returns.

edits.before: If Aurora opens the score, reset expectations and respect Across the Veil (Hop) doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: If Aurora opens the score her spirit healing makes every extended trade worse — buy Oblivion Orb instead of out-chipping it. After a second, farm from 1100 and only fight with your jungler on top of her.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the blink: Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1, and every window it is down is a free root, a free laser, and a dead Aurora.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Aurora off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, hold the lead with anti-heal and range: Oblivion Orb kills her spirit sustain, and a root inside her 22s blink window ends her before she lands.

edits.before: You start ahead: your E out-ranges Aurora's Q (Twofold Hex) poke and you punish her when she steps to proc her spirit passive on the wave. Levels 1-2 you poke freely, but once she has W (Across the Sand) blink she can dodge your Q and reposition, so the lane shifts toward even as she gains mobility.
edits.after: You start ahead: your E out-ranges Aurora's Q (Twofold Hex) poke and you punish her when she steps to proc her spirit passive on the wave. Levels 1-2 you poke freely, but once she has W (Across the Veil) blink she can dodge your Q and reposition, so the lane evens out — but it is 22s at rank 1, and that gap is your window.

edits.before: Aurora spikes at 6: her R (The Weystone) creates a zone and gives her a second blink, so she can W-in, combo, and W-out or R-reposition around your telegraphed skillshots. Her all-in with the double-blink beats your immobile poke now, so hold Flash and don't get zoned into her R field.
edits.after: Aurora spikes at 6: her R (Between Worlds) creates a zone and gives her a second blink, so she can W-in, combo, and W-out or R-reposition around your telegraphed skillshots. Her all-in with the double-blink beats your immobile poke now, so hold Flash — that R is 140s at rank 1 if she misses.

notes: Aurora's Between Worlds has a listed range of 250 in the kit — that is the leap, not the zone, so I avoided quoting a range for the R and quoted only its 140s rank-1 cooldown. Spirit Abjuration's heal amount is not in Riot's text, so the anti-heal advice names Oblivion Orb without claiming a magnitude. breakdown.wave was judged templated (the 'bus schedule' / 'most quoted death' phrasing is enemy-agnostic) but I could not ground a replacement in her kit inside the length band, so it was left alone.
